meeting_header:
Date: 2026-08-18 | Start: 15:30 PDT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Khatri (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (VectraLogic Head of ML), Owen Patel (VectraLogic Platform), Lena Ruiz (VectraLogic FinOps), Carlos Jimenez (VectraLogic Security)
summary: Mid-pilot checkpoint to triage runway risk: cost exposure, latency regressions, network constraints. Agreed next steps: run dedicated pool benchmark, share corpus, exchange security docs, and firm pilot commercial terms.
topics: pilot scope | latency SLOs | cost projection | VPC / KMS / SOC2 | model rollforward and fallbacks | autoscale and burst policy
transcript: [00:00] Jordan: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving time, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on VectraLogic, we also have Priya our SE and Samir from CS. Maya: hi everyone, thanks. [00:14] Jordan: quick agenda — 1) current pilot health and any surprise costs 2) infra constraints 3) finalizing rollforward plan and 4) next steps. Does that sound right? Maya: yeah that's good. [00:28] Priya: I'll kick off with the numbers we saw last 72 hours — overall token volume steady, but we noticed tail latency spikes on longer contexts during load windows. p95 around 420ms on hosted route, p99 closer to 1.2s on some long sequence paths. We're guessing KV cache misses and batching jitter. [00:45] Owen: yeah we saw the same from our telemetry — when the user flows hit the long multi-turn context, the cost per request went up and the FinOps dashboard freaked out a bit. Lena: yeah cost spike — we had a surprise 18% bump last night in our projected monthly burn. Not ideal. [01:05] Jordan: understood. On the cost side, there are three levers: routing to cheaper model variants, quantization profiles, and batching/caching policies. For the pilot you picked Dedicated pool yes? Maya: we requested dedicated but for the first week we used hosted while evaluating. We want predictable tail latencies and data isolation, so dedicated looks preferable. [01:30] Priya: dedicated will reduce variance; with pinned capacity and continuous batching we can hit p95 under 300ms for the target model given the right batch sizes and KV cache hit rate. But dedicated has sizing tradeoffs — small pool means you lose some efficiency. [01:47] Owen: question — if we go dedicated, how does burst work? We have occasional marketing spikes. Do we have automatic fallback to hosted? Jordan: yes, Redwood supports policy-based routing: primary dedicated pool, overflow to hosted or cheaper variant in a different region. We can define burst budget and throttle rules. [02:10] Maya: security is top of mind — we need KMS integration and audit logs. Carlos: also need SOC2 artifacts and proof of HSM-backed key storage or at least BYOK flow. [02:25] Jordan: we have SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes — we'll share links after the call. For private deployments (VPC/on-prem) we can do customer-managed keys, HSM via partner integrations, and ship audit logs to your SIEM. [02:42] Carlos: good, can you confirm log retention and whether Redwood supports SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning? [02:50] Priya: yes, SAML/SSO supported, SCIM for provisioning users, and audit log retention configurable — default 90 days, can be extended as an enterprise add-on. We'll include specifics in the security doc. [03:05] Lena: on pricing, we need a projection. The last run shows a 18% bump from what we expected — can you show an optimized config that meets our p95 target but keeps cost within a 10% delta? Jordan: short answer yes, we can model a few configurations. For example, 1) Dedicated + 8:1 batching + 4-bit quantization profile = lower per-token cost but initial infra commit; 2) Hosted with routing to smaller model for non-critical flows = less committed cost but more variable latency. We'll send cost model spreadsheet. [03:40] Owen: important: our infra requires specific outbound ranges and we have strict firewall rules. If we route to hosted fallback, do we need extra egress rules? Priya: if fallback hits hosted endpoints in public cloud, you'll need opening to Redwood egress IP ranges — alternatively we can peer via VPC peering where available. Owen: we'll prefer peering. [04:05] Maya: timeline — we want to decide by end of next week. We need runway confidence for Q4. [04:12] Jordan: agreed — pilot decision by 2026-08-27 is reasonable. Let's talk about the benchmark run specifics. Priya: for the benchmark we need a representative corpus (anonymized), expected concurrency pattern, and max sequence lengths. If you can provide (Owen) the typical concurrency histogram and 95th sequence length distribution, we can shape batch sizes and kernel selection. [04:40] Owen: I'll share that. We have a spike pattern: baseline 50rps, peak 320rps for ~4 hours. Sequence length p95 ~ 1,200 tokens. [04:55] Priya: 1,200 is on the higher side — that explains the p99 blowups. For long sequences we recommend aggressive prefix/KV caching and a model variant with attention kernels optimized for long context, or chunking user flows where possible. [05:12] Lena: about model rollforward — we want to be able to move to newer provider models without reworking app code. How does Redwood handle compatibility and fallback? Jordan: Redwood supports model variants and automatic fallback policies — you can pin a model version and set a rollout policy with canary slices. If a new model degrades quality or latency we can auto-fallback to a previous pinned version. Also we surface eval metrics to catch regressions. [05:40] Maya: what's our risk if we rollforward mid-Q4 during high traffic? Jordan: risk is higher for immediate rollouts — recommended staged canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% with monitoring for latency, token cost, and accuracy on a key prompt set. Priya: we'll tie regression alerts to your prompt set so any quality drop hits the on-call. [06:02] Owen: two technical items — 1) do we have GPU type guidance? 2) does Redwood runtime support mixed-precision quantization we can control? Priya: yes; for long context throughput we recommend A100 or equivalent with NVLink for bigger KV caches. Runtime supports int8 and 4-bit quantization profiles; we can tune per-model. [06:26] Carlos: about auditability — can you provide sample audit logs and a mapping of events (inference request, cache evict, rollout)? Priya: yes, we'll include an event schema and sample logs in the security pack. [06:40] Samir: just to surface a customer health item — we flagged that the pilot still hasn't hit a deterministic cost floor; FinOps worried. The action here is a controlled benchmark plus cost model. [06:55] Maya: agreed. We also want a short emergency runbook — if p99 crosses 2s in production, what's the immediate mitigation? Jordan: immediate mitigation steps: 1) throttle non-critical routes, 2) route to cheaper model variant, 3) increase dedicated pool if burst budget allows, 4) revert rollforward if pattern aligns with new model. We'll draft a short operational runbook. [07:25] Lena: can you include cost guardrails in the runbook? Jordan: yes, include token budget alarms and automatic route downgrade thresholds. [07:40] Priya: practical item: for the benchmark we plan two passes — synthetic stress test (no PII) and replay of anonymized real traffic. The replay will surface real batching and prefix patterns. We need your anonymized corpus and a signed data handling attestation. [07:58] Owen: we'll produce the corpus and attestation. [08:05] Maya: okay let's recap next steps. [08:09] Jordan: recap — Redwood to share security pack + SOC2 notes + KMS/HSM options; Redwood (Priya) to run dedicated pool benchmark and send latency histogram; Redwood (Jordan) to send cost projection spreadsheet and pilot commercial terms; VectraLogic (Owen) to share network CIDR and corpus; VectraLogic (Carlos) to list compliance docs needed. [08:35] Lena: thanks. Any blockers? Maya: not from our side, just timing and the corpus. [08:42] Jordan: great — we'll target the dates mentioned. Thanks everyone. [08:46] Priya: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window. [08:50] call ends
notes: Transcript contains minor transcription errors (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache, 'H S M' spaced tokens). Customer emphasized runway risk and explicit cost guardrails. Agreement to run two-pass benchmark and exchange security docs.
references: Pilot cost projection spreadsheet (shared after call)
